newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via customer/system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via customer/system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Monday via customer or system repurchase agreements, economists said.
At 0950 EDT/1350 GMT, the overnight bank lending, or federal funds rate, was trading at 5-3/16 percent, fractionally below the Fed's 5.25-percent target for the rate.
"They'll be in," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and an economist at Dean Witter Reynolds Inc. "It's a 50/50 chance of whether it will be a customer or a system," he said.
On Friday, fed funds closed at 4.875 percent after averaging 5.04 percent and trading at 3.0 to 5.25 percent.
